text:
Henry T. Brown (1908), movement 49:
Alternate circular motion of the horizontal shaft produces a continuous rotary motion of the vertical shaft, by means of the ratchet-wheels secured to the bevel-gears, the ratchet-teeth of the two wheels being set opposite ways, and the pawls acting in opposite directions. The bevel-gears and ratchet-wheels are loose on the shaft, and the pawls attached to arms firmly secured on the shaft.
provenance: Henry T. Brown, Five Hundred and Seven Mechanical Movements, 21st edition (1908), movement 49; public-domain excerpt. Transcription: https://507movements.com/mm_049.html.

text:
Henry T. Brown (1908), movement 75:
Reciprocating rectilinear motion of the rod, C, transmits an intermittent circular motion to the wheel, A, by means of the pawl, B, at the end of the vibrating-bar, D.
provenance: Henry T. Brown, Five Hundred and Seven Mechanical Movements, 21st edition (1908), movement 75; public-domain excerpt. Transcription: https://507movements.com/mm_075.html.

text:
Henry T. Brown (1908), movement 76:
A tappet, B, supported on the fixed pivot, C, is struck at every revolution of the large wheel (partly represented) by a stud, D, attached to the said wheel. This causes the end of the tappet next the ratchet-wheel, A, to be lifted, and to turn the wheel the distance of one tooth. The tappet returns by its own weight to its original position after the stud, D, has passed, the end being jointed to permit it to pass the teeth of the ratchet-wheel.
provenance: Henry T. Brown, Five Hundred and Seven Mechanical Movements, 21st edition (1908), movement 76; public-domain excerpt. Transcription: https://507movements.com/mm_076.html.

text:
Henry T. Brown (1908), movement 79:
Reciprocating rectilinear motion of the rod, B, produces a nearly continuous rotary movement of the ratchet-faced wheel, A, by the pawls attached to the extremities of the vibrating radial arms, C, C.
provenance: Henry T. Brown, Five Hundred and Seven Mechanical Movements, 21st edition (1908), movement 79; public-domain excerpt. Transcription: https://507movements.com/mm_079.html.

text:
Henry T. Brown (1908), movement 80:
Rectilinear motion is imparted to the slotted bar, A, by the vibration of the lever, C, through the agency of the two hooked pawls, which drop alternately into the teeth of the slotted rack-bar, A.
provenance: Henry T. Brown, Five Hundred and Seven Mechanical Movements, 21st edition (1908), movement 80; public-domain excerpt. Transcription: https://507movements.com/mm_080.html.

text:
Henry T. Brown (1908), movement 81:
Alternate rectilinear motion is given to the rack-rod, B, by the continuous revolution of the mutilated spur-gear, A, the spiral spring, C, forcing the rod back to its original position on the teeth of the gear, A, quitting the rack.
provenance: Henry T. Brown, Five Hundred and Seven Mechanical Movements, 21st edition (1908), movement 81; public-domain excerpt. Transcription: https://507movements.com/mm_081.html.

text:
Henry T. Brown (1908), movement 82:
On motion being given to the two treadles, D, a nearly continuous motion is imparted, through the vibrating arms, B, and their attached pawls, to the ratchet-wheel, A. A chain or strap attached to each treadle passes over the pulley, C, and as one treadle is depressed the other is raised.
provenance: Henry T. Brown, Five Hundred and Seven Mechanical Movements, 21st edition (1908), movement 82; public-domain excerpt. Transcription: https://507movements.com/mm_082.html.

text:
Henry T. Brown (1908), movement 206:
A continuous circular movement of the ratchet-wheel, produced by the vibration of the lever carrying two pawls, one of which engages the ratchet-teeth in rising and the other in falling.
provenance: Henry T. Brown, Five Hundred and Seven Mechanical Movements, 21st edition (1908), movement 206; public-domain excerpt. Transcription: https://507movements.com/mm_206.html.

text:
Henry T. Brown (1908), movement 225:
Intermittent circular motion of the ratchet-wheel from vibratory motion of the arm carrying a pawl.
provenance: Henry T. Brown, Five Hundred and Seven Mechanical Movements, 21st edition (1908), movement 225; public-domain excerpt. Transcription: https://507movements.com/mm_225.html.

text:
Henry T. Brown (1908), movement 236:
A nearly continuous circular motion is imparted to the ratchet-wheel on vibrating the lever, a, to which are attached the two pawls, b and c.
provenance: Henry T. Brown, Five Hundred and Seven Mechanical Movements, 21st edition (1908), movement 236; public-domain excerpt. Transcription: https://507movements.com/mm_236.html.

text:
Henry T. Brown (1908), movement 351:
Stamp. Vertical percussive falls derived from horizontal rotating shaft. The mutilated toothed pinion acts upon the rack to raise the rod until its teeth leave the rack and allow the rod to fall.
provenance: Henry T. Brown, Five Hundred and Seven Mechanical Movements, 21st edition (1908), movement 351; public-domain excerpt. Transcription: https://507movements.com/mm_351.html.
